endorsements.statement: Willamette Week endorsed Tina Kotek for governor.
endorsements.excerpt: We are once again endorsing Gov. Tina Kotek over state Sen. Christine Drazan, just as we did four years ago.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week endorsed Jeff Merkley for U.S. Senate.
endorsements.excerpt: Merkley has fought for this day during long, bleak months when it looked like Trump’s dark vision of blood-and-soil nationalism couldn’t be curtailed. He has earned a chance to hold Trump to account.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week endorsed Suzanne Bonamici for U.S. House District 1.
endorsements.excerpt: That’s a hard pass on Kahl. Voters should feel confident giving the incumbent two more years in Washington.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week endorsed Janelle Bynum for U.S. House District 5.
endorsements.excerpt: Adair wouldn’t comment on whether she thought Chavez-DeRemer’s conduct as labor secretary was disqualifying, dodged a question about her support for President Trump, and said Oregon’s guarantee of a right to abortion was not in line with her personal views, though she was glad abortion was back to being a state issue. Vote Bynum.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week endorsed Andrea Salinas for U.S. House District 6.
endorsements.excerpt: Salinas projects competence and a level head. She’s earned another two years in D.C.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week endorsed Courtney Neron Misslin for Oregon Senate District 13.
endorsements.excerpt: Neron Misslin has big goals for our most vexing societal problems—in education, health care and the environment—and she’s demonstrated a willingness to put in the work, despite long odds. She’s the clear choice for District 13.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week endorsed Myrna Muñoz for Oregon Senate District 15.
endorsements.excerpt: Muñoz has behaved unprofessionally, and this doesn’t bode well for what could ultimately be a long, strange tenure in the Oregon Senate. But she seems a reliable vote on issues she’s passionate about: civil rights, education and health care.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week endorsed Rachel Armitage for Oregon Senate District 16.
endorsements.excerpt: Having kept her promise and sat out for four years, Armitage now represents the best choice for this seat.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week endorsed Lisa Reynolds for Oregon Senate District 17.
endorsements.excerpt: But for now, she has shown herself to be a practical leader and a clear communicator. Reynolds is the obvious choice.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week endorsed Rob Wagner for Oregon Senate District 19.
endorsements.excerpt: But we aren’t deciding Senate leadership—just this race. In that regard, Wagner is the better choice.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week endorsed Mark Meek for Oregon Senate District 20.
endorsements.excerpt: Meek is proving to be a more than sufficient form of loyal opposition.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week endorsed Jeff Helfrich for Oregon Senate District 26.
endorsements.excerpt: We wish Bassett had run for the open seat in House District 52. In this matchup, however, Helfrich is the best choice.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week endorsed Ben Bowman for Oregon House District 25.
endorsements.excerpt: Bowman is learning hard lessons and has our glowing endorsement.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week endorsed Tammy Carpenter for Oregon House District 27.
endorsements.excerpt: Carpenter’s politics better match her district, and we give her the nod, though with the caveat that she could well end up as another lawmaker in the pocket of unions that tend to conflate—sometimes inaccurately—their own interest with the public’s.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week endorsed Dacia Grayber for Oregon House District 28.
endorsements.excerpt: Grayber’s served here for three terms, and we think she’s the clear choice for a fourth.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week endorsed Brian Schimmel for Oregon House District 29.
endorsements.excerpt: He’s gathered endorsements from the mayors of Hillsboro, Forest Grove and Cornelius, which suggests McLain has lost touch with her district. Vote for Schimmel.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week endorsed Tom Forest for Oregon House District 31.
endorsements.excerpt: We give the edge—quite narrowly, it should be said—to Forest, who has the potential to learn on the job.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week endorsed Shannon Isadore for Oregon House District 33.
endorsements.excerpt: Isadore has capably represented District 33 for two years and ought to have two more.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week endorsed Hai Pham for Oregon House District 36.
endorsements.excerpt: Given Pham’s experience, education and track record in Salem, voters should feel comfortable giving him a third term.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week endorsed Jules Walters for Oregon House District 37.
endorsements.excerpt: Since Jules Walters arrived in Salem after stints as the mayor and a city councilor for West Linn, the former baker and cook has achieved notable legislative clout.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week endorsed Michael Sugar for Oregon House District 40.
endorsements.excerpt: Baker’s no slouch, but we found it significant that Sugar got the endorsements of all three mayors in the district, the chamber of commerce, and several prominent unions. We’ll add our name to that list.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week endorsed Mark Gamba for Oregon House District 41.
endorsements.excerpt: Still, a more administratively simplified, muscular government would, in fact, be a productive engine for better lives, and Gamba is a serious champion for this cause. The people of Oregon House District 41 should send him back to Salem.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week endorsed Rob Nosse for Oregon House District 42.
endorsements.excerpt: Nosse is the clear choice in this race.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week endorsed Tawna Sanchez for Oregon House District 43.
endorsements.excerpt: Still, Sanchez is the most qualified candidate for this seat.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week endorsed Lamar Wise for Oregon House District 48.
endorsements.excerpt: Wise isn’t a great choice. But he’s better than Morrison.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week endorsed Zach Hudson for Oregon House District 49.
endorsements.excerpt: Hudson didn’t wow us, but he made a persuasive case that he is in fact attuned to the needs of his constituents, and correctly pointed out that it is Democrats like him who tend to favor rent caps.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week endorsed Darla Mead for Oregon House District 51.
endorsements.excerpt: Mead’s campaign has been plainly outraised—the Democrats put resources where they think they can win—but she can claim serious endorsements and has a bolder, more compelling vision for the structural role Salem could play in improving the lives of her neighbors and her patients. Give her a shot.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week endorsed Scott Hege for Oregon House District 52.
endorsements.excerpt: Hege, by contrast, has a strong grasp on his district’s needs, and having a Republican voice in the Legislature that has deep knowledge of the industries and economics that buoy his district is a better bet than a slick Democratic scion who repeats party lines with little substance. Vote for Hege.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week endorsed Laura Maurer Rowan for Multnomah County Circuit Court, Position 2.
endorsements.excerpt: Maurer Rowan has seven years of experience in litigating criminal cases, and observers we spoke to say she’s an active listener, a critical skill for a judge. Vote for Maurer Rowan.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week endorsed Elizabeth Savage for Multnomah County Circuit Court, Position 14.
endorsements.excerpt: After two rounds of interviews, combined with her experience and endorsements, Savage has emerged as the stronger candidate for the job.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week ranked Shannon Singleton #1 for Multnomah County chair.
endorsements.excerpt: We suggest they rank all three of the main candidates—but give the top spot to Shannon Singleton.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week ranked Julia Brim-Edwards #2 for Multnomah County chair.
endorsements.excerpt: Julia Brim-Edwards is still our second choice for chair.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week ranked Sharon Meieran #3 for Multnomah County chair.
endorsements.excerpt: Our final pick for chair is Sharon Meieran, who came in second to no one in the competition to irritate Vega Pederson.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week ranked Bri Williams #1 for Multnomah County Commissioner District 2.
endorsements.excerpt: We are narrowly giving our top endorsement to Bri Williams, a county employee launching a progressive bid for the seat.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week ranked Serena Cruz #2 for Multnomah County Commissioner District 2.
endorsements.excerpt: We think Cruz’s priorities are clear in this contest—and the correct ones. She wants to more clearly define the roles of the county, the city, and Metro on homeless services, and she’s come around to the idea of an accountability system to hold each government to its respective tasks.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week ranked Steve Novick #1 for Portland City Council District 3.
endorsements.excerpt: Our top choice to return to council for a full four-year term is Steve Novick.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week ranked Tiffany Koyama Lane #2 for Portland City Council District 3.
endorsements.excerpt: Koyama Lane, 40, has also approached the budget process with a fine-toothed comb rather than an ax, which shows an attention to detail sometimes lacking on this council.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week ranked Kellie Torres #3 for Portland City Council District 3.
endorsements.excerpt: We didn’t find her all that inspiring, nor were her policy ideas terribly original, but we think she’ll provide a common-sense vote to safeguard the city’s basic services from budget cuts as the city approaches another $100 million-plus deficit.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week ranked Cristal Otero #4 for Portland City Council District 3.
endorsements.excerpt: She’s like a skilled plumber, but for homelessness spending. We would rank her fourth.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week ranked Angelita Morillo #5 for Portland City Council District 3.
endorsements.excerpt: We see the results—a coarsening of civic life—and rank her fifth.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week ranked Olivia Clark #1 for Portland City Council District 4.
endorsements.excerpt: We ranked Clark, 72, as our first choice in the 2024 election. She’s earned that spot again with her straightforward manner, lack of drama, and courage to champion a new street fee that will help fund the Portland Bureau of Transportation in the face of a collective groan from Portlanders already feeling overtaxed and underserved.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week ranked Eric Zimmerman #2 for Portland City Council District 4.
endorsements.excerpt: Eric Zimmerman, 42, is our second choice.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week ranked Jayne Cronlund #3 for Portland City Council District 4.
endorsements.excerpt: For our third choice, we’re taking a chance on Jayne Cronlund, a land preservationist, member of the Oregon State Bar, and owner of a small business that advises nonprofit organizations on staff retention and preventing burnout.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week ranked Mitch Green #4 for Portland City Council District 4.
endorsements.excerpt: Councilors must play by the rules they set. We find his blasé attitude toward those rules disqualifying for a top-three spot.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week ranked Eli Arnold #5 for Portland City Council District 4.
endorsements.excerpt: Still, there could be worse things than Arnold sitting on the council. He gets our fifth-place nod.

endorsements.statement: Willamette Week endorsed a No vote on Portland Measure 26-267 (participatory budgeting).
endorsements.excerpt: This is a poorly written measure. Vote no.

notes: All 7 source files read in full. Ranked races (Multnomah chair, Commissioner D2, Portland Council D3 and D4) have one entry per ranked candidate. Rank order for Cruz (D2 #2) is inferred from listing order plus 'rank the two'; Mitch Green (D4 #4) is inferred from 'we rank him above Eli Arnold' and Arnold's explicit fifth place. Koyama Lane and Torres (D3) ranks 2 and 3 come from the sentence 'the result would be Novick, Koyama Lane and Torres'; each entry now carries its own candidate-specific excerpt (verified 2026-10-15). HD 29 Brian Schimmel: WW labels him 'Republican/Independent' (Independent Party member who also won the Republican nomination); inventory lists him as Independent. Entries carry no party field, so no change was needed. Esther Leon, Jamey Evenstar and Tom Sollitt were explicitly not ranked in D3/D4. HD 28 Randall Fryer, HD 36 Orth etc. not endorsed. Several endorsements are lukewarm (Muñoz SD15, Wise HD48, Meek SD20, Forest HD31) but explicit. Sykes and Hagedorn were not endorsed in the general. No 'none' or 'dual' picks.
